claim_boundary: Dispatch-time critical-source revalidation is internal effect-safety and context-control evidence. It does not demonstrate useful behavioral improvement, independent production capability, AGI, or the user's upper objective.
evidence_needed: effect plan and authorization records bind the exact verified manifest digest, semantic request identity, action digest, and critical-source projection used at authorization
a dispatch-time recheck occurs after typed authorization validation and immediately before any dispatch claim or provider callback

heartbeat-only refresh under the same live generation, execution, fence, status, inbox revision, policy, and action constraints remains valid while stale heartbeat, lease/fence/status change, inbox revision or effective-policy change, and action mismatch fail closed
the provider callback and dispatch claim are both absent when the critical recheck fails
an exact completed replay performs no provider side effect and remains replayable even after later control-state changes
no raw fence token, secret, unbounded source payload, or outer-session memory is copied into effect records
protected manifest, effect, reconciliation, adjudication, monitor, lifecycle, and immutable replay tests plus exact-head publication evidence
expected_outputs: a bounded critical dispatch-context projection and verifier owned by the Context Kernel
effect plan, authorization, typed capability, and dispatch integration that binds and rechecks that projection
focused revocation-after-authorization, stale-heartbeat, heartbeat-refresh, no-callback/no-claim, completed-replay, and tamper tests
updated Context Kernel architecture, strategy, continuation, and native O records
isolated exact-head CI, conflict-free expected-head merge, reviewed-blob readback, and explicit negative evidence
failure_conditions: a provider callback can run after a critical lease, user, policy, or action-constraint revocation
a failed recheck persists a dispatch claim or calls the provider
ordinary same-owner heartbeat refresh invalidates an otherwise identical live authorization
a completed effect is redispatched or becomes unreplayable solely because later control state changed
frozen Work requests or historical effect records are retroactively rewritten
raw secrets, raw fence tokens, or unbounded external context enter the critical projection
internal dispatch safety is reported as behavioral capability, AGI, or completion
goal: Bind every newly authorized Work external effect to the exact O DecisionContextManifest and fail closed immediately before provider dispatch when the current critical lease, user-revocation, effective-directive, or action-constraint state no longer matches the authorization boundary, without mutating frozen requests or weakening completed-effect replay.
inputs: merged PR 279 semantic-component DecisionContextManifest construction and verification
src/continual/work_effects.py effect plan and authorization records
src/continual/work_effect_dispatch.py typed authorization and provider callback boundary
agi/WORK_EXECUTION_STATE.json lease generation, execution, fence digest, status, and heartbeat contract
agi/USER_INPUT_INBOX.json and agi/USER_DIRECTIVE_EVENTS.json current revision and effective policy
tests/test_work_effect_dispatch.py and protected Context Kernel/effect lifecycle regressions
parent_continuation: After Execute, Task Evaluate the exact authorization binding, temporal ordering, revocation cases, replay behavior, CI, merge, readback, and negative evidence; then Consolidate Episode and Learn. Return to Root for the next falsifiable context-control or held-out behavioral unit.
rollback: Retain the merged semantic-component manifests and existing fail-closed typed effect stack; leave this branch unmerged if the critical projection cannot distinguish safe heartbeat renewal from authority or policy revocation, changes frozen history, or weakens completed-effect idempotency.
